status_summary: Executive Order 14184 (2025-01-27) directed reinstatement at former rank with back pay and benefits, and DOD announced an outreach program on 2025-04-23 for roughly 8,700 separated members (a July 2026 report puts involuntary separations at nearly 8,000). Uptake has been small: 13 had returned by late June 2025, and in July 2026 the Pentagon put returns at about 230, while a 2026-07-23 report gave about 200 troops and 85 Coast Guard members reinstated, nearly 900 discharge upgrades, and more than 800 who had expressed interest. The window to rejoin was extended on 2026-03-23 to 2027-04-01 with the returnee service obligation cut from four years to two, and a Secretary of War memorandum dated 2026-05-07 extends the expedited reinstatement program by one year, directs correction boards to treat discharges preceded only by vaccine-refusal-related adverse actions as unjust, and offers discharge upgrades and repayment of recouped bonuses to those who do not return, without addressing rank or back pay. Under DOD policy back pay is reduced by interim civilian income and VA payments, and some applicants described waits of months to over a year.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14184 signed. It directs DOD and DHS to offer reinstatement at former rank with full back pay, benefits, and bonuses to members discharged solely for refusing the vaccine, and to report progress within 60 days.
Secretary Hegseth announces the reinstatement outreach program at the Army War College; roughly 8,700 members are eligible and the offer is to stay open one year.
Reporting finds only 13 former members had returned to service after the outreach and back-pay offer.
Hegseth extends the invitation to return to 2027-04-01 and cuts the active-service commitment for returnees from four years to two.

A Secretary of War memorandum to the Secretaries of the Military Departments and the Chief of the National Guard Bureau extends the expedited reinstatement program by one year and directs correction boards to evaluate petitioners for unjust discharge, treating adverse actions tied solely to vaccine refusal that led to separation as grounds; it offers record corrections and discharge upgrades to those who do not return. It does not address rank or back pay and prints no calendar end date.

A Pentagon official says about 230 former members have rejoined (about 2.7 percent of those eligible) and that more than 600 have expressed interest. DOD announces a panel to study the mandate decision and to declassify related materials.
Military Times reports roughly 200 troops and 85 Coast Guard members reinstated, nearly 900 discharge upgrades, back pay reduced by offsets, and delays for some applicants.

title: Reinstate members discharged over the COVID-19 vaccine, with rank and back pay
uncertainties: Counts differ between Military Times reports (about 230 rejoined on 2026-07-16 versus about 200 troops plus 85 Coast Guard members a week later); they were not reconciled. Official Navy and Air Force pages read on 2026-10-26 describe the remedies: the Air Force release of 2025-04-07 (af.mil) says the Boards for Correction of Military Records may order restoration of rank and credit for lost service time, with a four-year service commitment (later cut to two years by the 2026-03-23 extension) and 60 days to accept after a compensation estimate, and the Navy's MyNavy HR reinstatement page (no date printed) says involuntarily separated members may be eligible for back pay, benefits, bonus payments or other compensation subject to required offsets, with DFAS to determine the back pay package within 90 days of submission, and that voluntary separations receive no back pay. Neither page gives a count of reinstated members or says whether rank has been restored or back pay paid in any case, so whether back pay has been paid in full rests on news reports. A DOD News article of 2025-04-24 posted on jbsa.mil reports that the Secretary signed a memorandum ordering additional remedies that day, one day after the 2025-04-23 outreach announcement; it does not mention back pay, rank or counts, and the memorandum itself was not opened. The May 2026 memorandum was opened on media.defense.gov as extracted text with a garbled date stamp, read as 2026-05-07 (the URL path shows 2026-05-08, and a second copy attached to a Federal Circuit filing on kneselaw.com shows the same stamp); it does not mention rank, back pay or a calendar end date and describes the extension only as one year, so its end date relative to the 2027-04-01 window was not determined. The filing date of that court copy is taken from its file name because the document shows none, and the filing, an appeal in which the memorandum is offered as supplemental authority, was not read beyond the exhibit. The 2025-06-30 return count comes from a search-result headline and snippet that was not opened. The Military.com and Military Times pieces are news reports; no court challenge to this program itself was found. Update 2026-10-15: one search for post-July figures returned only earlier reports.
